title: Add Pareto failure-signature gate and automated rollback playbook
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: We observed recurring long-tail failures during nightly prompt-set smoke runs where a small number of prompts accounted for the majority of degradation incidents across multiple models. This PR introduces a Pareto failure-signature gate that flags small-high-impact prompt subsets and couples it with an automated rollback playbook to reduce noisy pager events and speed incident remediation. Summary of changes: 1) pareto_signatures module: algorithm to compute 80/20-style failure signatures across evaluation cohorts with temporal weighting and minimum-sample thresholds; 2) gate adapter: CI hook that runs after comparative evals and fails builds when the signature severity score exceeds configurable SLOs; 3) rollback-playbook: a templated operations playbook that can be triggered automatically (or manually) to roll back model routes and schedule a minimock backfill evaluation; 4) dashboards: small telemetry additions to expose signature counts and trend deltas; 5) docs and unit tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement pareto scoring and severity bucketing - [x] Add CI hook wiring and gate configuration - [x] Add rollback playbook and automated trigger (with opt-out) - [x] Unit tests and smoke tests - [x] Docs for on-call and release engineering Impact and rationale: The gate is conservative by default (high threshold) and designed to reduce noisy, low-signal failures while catching concentrated regressions that affect business-critical prompt groups. The rollback playbook automates safe steps (route freeze, route pin to previous model, backfill evaluation) and emits a structured incident note for SRE. Configuration knobs are exposed in eval config with clear defaults. Backwards compatibility: No changes to existing eval Graph API surface; gate is opt-in via linear keys in the repo eval config. Testing: Local unit tests cover scoring, threshold math, and playbook rendering. End-to-end smoke runs added to the nightly pipeline and validated in staging. Rollout plan: Feature flag off by default; enable for internal-canary prompt-sets for two weeks, then opt-in across production smoke cohorts. Security: Playbook actions that change routing require a RBAC token and explicit approval in enterprise installs. Implementation notes: Pareto signature uses aggregated failure fingerprints derived from failure type, prompt-id hash, and model-variant tag. Temporal weighting uses an exponential decay window with parameterizable half-life. CI hook runs as a post-eval step with a best-effort backoff and will not block if dependency services are unreachable (it will mark CI as pending and create a ticket). See linked Linear tasks for rollout timeline and telemetry dashboards.

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice approach; can you clarify how the signature dedup window avoids double-counting when prompt IDs are canonicalized?
Priya Shah: We hash prompt text then attach model-variant namespace; dedup window is 12 hours by default, configurable in eval config.
Samantha Ortiz: The rollback playbook should require a secondary human approval in prod. Suggest adding a hard stop for orgs without automated rollbacks.
Priya Shah: Agreed; playbook has a default manual-approval step for production and an opt-in automated flag for internal teams.
Evan Green: CI hook added an external dependency on the telemetry API; what happens on transient failures?
Priya Shah: Hook will not block merges on telemetry timeouts; it records a pending state and creates a ticket for follow-up. We added retries with exponential backoff and observability counters.
notes: Backported small fix to staging pipeline after CI flake; merged after approvals and green CI. Rollout gated by Linear ENG-2109 and monitored via new dashboard widgets.
